# Kvasir — Decentralized AI Inference (full site text)

Source: https://kvasir-ai.net/ · Engine: https://github.com/louisevandan/kvasir-net (BSL) · Last updated: 2026-07-13

This file is a plain-text mirror of the Kvasir homepage for LLM ingestion. All
claims are grounded in the linkcpp / Kvasir codebase. Compliance note: KVR is a
utility / contribution token on Solana devnet — not a tradable asset, price, or
investment; nothing here is a promise of financial return.

## Brand system

- linkcpp — the source-available engine / control plane: a Dockerized control hub around inference engine's RPC data plane, plus a new peer-to-peer ring runtime. Discovers devices, plans layer placement, launches workers, exposes OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible gateways. Source-available under the Business Source License (BSL).
- Kvasir — the network / product brand: the non-custodial wallet + settlement gateway + node-reward network built on linkcpp.
- KVR — the token. On-chain name "Kvasir", 6 decimals, Solana (devnet today). Used to pay for inference and to reward contributors.

One line: linkcpp is the engine; Kvasir is the network that turns it into a rewarded, decentralized AI inference marketplace paid in KVR.

## Hero

Headline: Bring compute. Earn KVR.
Kvasir splits large open models across shared hardware with linkcpp, so no single node holds the whole model. Contribute a GPU, CPU, NPU — even a phone — and earn KVR for the layers you run.
Badges: Runs on GPU · CPU · NPU · phone · OpenAI + Anthropic compatible · BSL engine · Solana devnet.

## Why decentralized AI (thesis)

AI shouldn't be owned by a handful of companies. Frontier inference is concentrating behind a few walled datacenters — closed weights, metered access, one bill paid to one owner. Kvasir points the other way: open models served across a permissionless network of everyday devices, owned and earned by the people who run it.

Centralized AI: a few hyperscalers own the GPUs; models and infrastructure behind closed APIs; you rent access and value flows upward; opaque — you trust the operator.
Kvasir: any device joins a peer-to-peer ring — no central master; source-available linkcpp engine (BSL), inspectable; contributors earn KVR for the real compute they give; non-custodial — your keys, your node, your rewards.

## The name (origin)

In Norse mythology, Kvasir was born when the Æsir and Vanir gods ended their war and made peace: each spat into a single vessel, and from their pooled essence rose the wisest being who ever lived — one who could answer any question. When he was slain, his blood was brewed into the Mead of Poetry, a draught that granted wisdom to everyone who drank it.
Why the name: pooled from every god and owned by none → intelligence assembled from many contributors' devices, no single owner. The wisest being answering any question → an open inference network anyone can query. A mead that shared wisdom with all → open access and KVR rewards to every contributor. On-chain, the token is named Kvasir (KVR) — the mead, distributed.

## How it works

1. Split — the model is divided into contiguous layer windows. Every device stores the same model but loads only its window; no node holds the whole thing. (Qwen3.5-122B, 49 layers, rank manifest.)
2. Serve — the request enters the ring. Each node runs its layers and passes only the hidden-state boundary to its neighbor; the last node samples the token and sends it back around — no central master. (ring runtime, OpenAI/Anthropic compatible.)
3. Reward — each node earns KVR weighted by the layers it ran (its share of the tokens produced), settled on Solana to that node's own wallet. (units += (out_tokens / 1000) × layer_share.)

## For contributors

Turn idle compute into KVR. Point a supported device at the network and it starts serving layers. You earn KVR proportional to the layers your node runs — your keys stay in your own wallet. Non-custodial by design — operator login is a Sign-In With Solana wallet signature with optional 2FA.

- Any device can join: GPUs, CPUs, NPUs and phones all run layers today. A peer-to-peer ring runtime lets each device hold just a few layers and pass only small boundary state to its neighbor — no gatekeeper, no single owner.
- Layer-share rewards: proportional to the layers your node runs, not vague participation. 1 unit ≈ 1k tokens × your layer share of each inference.
- Performance tiers: measured throughput sets a tier — S (×1.5), A (×1.25), B (×1.0), C (×0.7) — that multiplies your earned units.
- Uptime for infra roles: nodes filling infrastructure roles also accrue hourly uptime rewards.

Supported devices: GPU (CUDA · ROCm · Metal · Vulkan), CPU (x86-64 · ARM), NPU (on-device accelerators), Mobile (phones & edge via the ring runtime).

## For developers

One endpoint, backed by many devices. Keep your existing OpenAI or Anthropic client, point it at the Kvasir gateway, and pay per inference in KVR — no rewrites.

- OpenAI-compatible: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/models
- Anthropic-compatible: /anthropic/v1/messages and /anthropic/v1/models
- Pay-per-inference in KVR: quote → payment → inference
- Live model catalog aggregated from reachable hubs

Example:
curl https://gate.kvasir-ai.net/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KVR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "model": "Qwen3.5-122B-A10B", "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "Explain layer-split inference." } ] }'

## Token & rewards (KVR)

KVR is the unit developers spend on inference and the unit contributors earn for the layers they run. Rewards are computed from real work, not participation.
- Symbol: KVR (on-chain name "Kvasir", 6 decimals). Chain: Solana (devnet today). Pays for: inference (pay-per-request via the gateway). Rewards: compute (layer-share × performance tier).
- Non-custodial wallet: rewards settle to each node's own owner wallet; keys live in the user's wallet (browser, desktop, or mobile), never with an operator. Wallets on web, desktop, iOS, Android.
- Devnet, utility token: KVR currently runs on Solana devnet and is a utility / contribution token — not a tradable asset, price, or investment. Nothing here is financial advice or a promise of return.

## Network roles & rewards

Every role in the network earns KVR. The ring of compute nodes is coordinated by hub and gateway roles; each is paid in KVR for what it actually does.
- Compute node (runs the model's layers): holds a few contiguous layers in the ring; earns per contribution unit (≈1k tokens served) × layer share × performance tier.
- Gateway host (public entry + settlement): serves the OpenAI/Anthropic gateway and settles KVR payments; earns hourly uptime + a ×1.5 bonus on every inference it helps serve.
- Hub host (the control plane): discovers devices, plans layer placement, orchestrates the ring; the most critical role, so it earns the highest hourly uptime reward.
Roles stack: one machine can be compute, gateway and hub at once, and its rewards sum together — all settled in KVR to that node's own wallet.

Reward math: units += (tokens / 1k) × (node_layers / total_layers); effective = units × perf_tier × gateway_bonus; infra roles also earn hourly uptime (hub rate > gateway rate), summed on top.
Performance tiers (by measured decode throughput): S ≥ 90 tok/s ×1.5; A ≥ 60 tok/s ×1.25; B ≥ 30 tok/s ×1.0; C < 30 tok/s ×0.7.

## Under the hood (linkcpp)

linkcpp is the open control hub that turns everyday hardware into a distributed inference engine. Its ring runtime lets each device hold only a few layers and pass hidden state to its neighbor — no central master — while the stock inference engine data plane stays unforked. linkcpp's own tagline: "Run large GGUF models across multiple GPUs and machines with stock inference engine binaries."
- Ring runtime: every device stores the same model and loads only its layer window, opening one link to its predecessor and one to its successor; hidden-state boundaries circulate around the ring and the last rank returns the token — no central master.
- linkcpp control hub: a single Dockerized hub — the control plane inference engine's RPC data plane was missing. Discovers devices, plans layer placement, launches the stock workers, exposes the gateways. Source-available under the Business Source License (BSL).
- Distributed layer placement: reads GGUF metadata and computes contiguous per-node layer windows via a rank manifest, plus optional MoE expert-FFN offload to node RAM.
- SIWS + 2FA security: for public deployments, operator access is a Sign-In With Solana signature over a server nonce, plus TOTP 2FA and single-use backup codes — on both hub and gateway.
The engine is source-available under the Business Source License (BSL): https://github.com/louisevandan/kvasir-net

## Roadmap

- Now — Any-device inference, live: GPUs, CPUs, NPUs and phones serve layers across the ring runtime. 122B ran split across 4 GPUs; contribution credited end-to-end; non-custodial wallets on web/desktop/iOS/Android; access secured on public domains.
- Coming — Mainnet & on-chain settlement: everything today runs on Solana devnet with an off-chain settlement service; an on-chain rewards program and mainnet are planned.
- Coming — A permissionless global network: current demos ran on one operator's hardware; opening the network so anyone, anywhere can plug in a device and earn (no gatekeeper) is next.

## Proof / traction

- 122B params served split across 4 AMD MI250 GPUs.
- 4 distinct owner wallets each earning their layer share.
- 2 API surfaces — OpenAI + Anthropic compatible.
- 4 wallet platforms — web · desktop · iOS · Android.
Summary: 122B served across 4 GPUs · OpenAI + Anthropic compatible · wallets on web/desktop/iOS/Android · live on public domains.

## Inference API — self-issue an API key (for agents)

A native OpenAI-compatible endpoint with a prepaid-credit API key. An AI agent holding a Solana wallet secret can obtain a key headlessly (no browser):

- Base URL: https://gate.kvasir-ai.net/v1 · Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>`
- Model: `f793eb7b:ctrl-f11eb9` (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B); `GET /v1/models` to list. Streaming (SSE) and native tool_calls are supported.
- SIWS signing: sign the challenge `message` string verbatim with the wallet's ed25519 key; submit the 64-byte signature as base64. `wallet` is the base58 public key.

Self-issue flow:
1. `POST https://gate.kvasir-ai.net/api/credits/register/challenge {"wallet":"<W>"}` -> `{nonce, message}`
2. sign(message) -> `POST /api/credits/register {"wallet","nonce","signature"}` (200 = self-registered onto the whitelist; 403 = self-register closed, an operator must approve)
3. `POST /api/credits/challenge {"wallet":"<W>"}` -> `{nonce, message}` (403 = not whitelisted)
4. sign(message) -> `POST /api/credits/apikey {"wallet","nonce","signature","label":"agent"}` -> `{apiKey}` (returned once — store it)
5. Use `apiKey` as an OpenAI Bearer key at the base URL. Check credit with `GET /api/credits/balance` (Bearer) -> `{balance, spent, symbol}`.

Pricing: `basePrice + tokens × perToken` KVR (currently `0.01 + tokens×0.00002`), Solana devnet. Insufficient balance -> HTTP 402; top up by transferring KVR to the treasury, then `POST /api/credits/deposit {wallet, amount, signature}`.
Runnable self-issue scripts (TS/Node, Python), the streaming + tool-call examples, and an interactive issuer are on the developer page: https://kvasir-ai.net/docs/api
